printed: 1. SHORT-TERM STATIONARY IS DAYTIME WORK THAT OCCUPIES A LOCATION FOR MORE THAN 1 HOUR WITHIN A SINGLE DAYLIGHT PERIOD
2. IN URBAN CONDITIONS, ADVANCE WARNING SIGN SPACINGS MAY BE ADJUSTED IN ORDER TO ACCOMMODATE SIDE STREETS AND DRIVEWAYS. IF THERE IS A CONFLICT, MOVE THE SIGN UPSTREAM. URBAN
3. THIS TYPICAL APPLICATION SHALL BE USED WITH RED/YELLOW LENS AUTOMATED FLAGGER ASSISTANCE DEVICES (AFAD). URBAN URBAN
4. AFADS SHALL ONLY BE USED IN SITUATIONS WHERE THERE IS ONLY ONE LANE OF APPROACHING RURAL TRAFFIC IN THE DIRECTION TO BE CONTROLLED

5. THE OPERATOR OF THE AFAD MAY BE LOCATED ANYWHERE WITHIN THE WORK ZONE UNDER THE FOLLOWING CONDITIONS: A. BE TRAINED ON THE OPERATION OF THE MODEL AFAD THEY ARE USING, B. HAVE AN UNOBSTRUCTED VIEW OF THE AFAD, C. HAVE AN UNOBSTRUCTED VIEW OF APPROACHING TRAFFIC IN BOTH DIRECTIONS, AND D. NOT LEAVE THE AFAD UNATTENDED AT ANY TIME WHILE THE AFAD IS BEING USED

6. THE AFAD SHALL BE PLACED ON THE SHOULDER ADJACENT TO THE TRAVEL LANE ENSURING THAT THE GATE ARM REACHES AT LEAST TO THE CENTER OF THE LANE BEING CONTROLLED. A 24"x24" RED FLAG SHOULD BE ATTACHED TO END OF GATE ARM TO INCREASE VISIBILITY
7. CENTERLINE CONES MAY BE ADDED TO ENHANCE THE VISIBILITY OF THE FLAGGER STATION. IF CONES ARE USED, PLACE THEM 100 FT. (MINIMUM) FROM AFAD
8. THE OPERATOR OF THE AFAD SHALL NOT DISPLAY THE AFAD'S OR YELLOW LENS PHASE UNTIL ALL ONCOMING VEHICLES HAVE CLEARED THE ONE-LANE PORTION OF THE WORK ZONE
9. "BE PREPARED TO STOP" SIGN (W3-4) AND "ONE LANE ROAD AHEAD" SIGN (W20-4) SHALL BE REMOVED, COVERED OR TURNED AWAY FROM ROAD USERS WHEN FLAGGING OPERATIONS ARE NOT OCCURRING

10. APPROPRIATE FLAGGER TOOLS (STOP/SLOW PADDLE, RED FLAG, HIGH VISIBILITY APPAREL, ETC.) SHALL BE ON-SITE, AVAILABLE AND READY TO USE IN THE EVENT OF AN AFAD MALFUNCTION OR TRAFFIC VOLUMES EXCEED THE CAPABILITY OF THE AFAD TO EFFECTIVELY CONTROL TRAFFIC

11. A SINGLE OPERATOR MAY SIMULTANEOUSLY CONTROL TWO AFADS AS LONG AS BOTH CONDITIONS ARE PRESENT: A. THE OPERATOR HAS AN UNOBSTRUCTED VIEW OF THE AFADS, AND B. THE OPERATOR HAS AN UNOBSTRUCTED VIEW OF APPROACHING TRAFFIC IN BOTH DIRECTIONS
12. IF THE AFAD IS NOT EQUIPPED WITH A R10-6 SIGN, ONE SHALL BE PLACED 8' IN ADVANCE OF THE AFAD. SIGN

13. THE AFAD SHALL BE CLEARLY VISIBLE TO THE FIRST APPROACHING ROAD USER AT ALL TIMES G20-2 AND SHOULD BE VISIBLE TO OTHER ROAD USERS. THE AFAD SHALL BE STATIONED SUFFICIENTLY IN ADVANCE OF THE WORKERS TO WARN THEM (FOR EXAMPLE, WITH AUDIBLE R10-6 WARNING DEVICES SUCH AS HORNS OR WHISTLES) OF APPROACHING DANGER BY OUT-OF-CONTROL/NON-COMPLIANT VEHICLES. THE AFAD SHALL STAND ALONE, AWAY FROM OTHER W3-4 WORKERS, WORK VEHICLES, OR EQUIPMENT. W20-1

14. AFAD SHALL BE POSITIONED IN ACCORDANCE WITH TABLE 309-05 TO ENSURE ADEQUATE W20-4 STOPPING SIGHT DISTANCE (X) FOR THE APPROACHING ROAD USERS. IF THE REQUIRED DISTANCE (X) CANNOT BE ACHIEVED DUE TO AN OBSTRUCTION CAUSED BY HORIZONTAL/VERTICAL CURVES OR OTHER FEATURES THEN THE ACTIVITY AREA SHOULD BE MODIFIED TO A POINT WHERE WARNING FLAG ADEQUATE STOPPING SIGHT DISTANCE CAN BE ACHIEVED OR PROTECTIVE VEHICLE SHALL BE *FREEWAY UTILIZED AS SHOWN ON DETAIL 309D

15. PROTECTIVE VEHICLE WITH APPROPRIATE ROLL AHEAD DISTANCE MAY BE USED IN ADVANCE OF THE WORK AREA, IF DEEMED NECESSARY BY THE DOT ENGINEER OR THEIR DESIGNEE. TO USE PROTECTIVE VEHICLE, SEE DETAIL 309D. WHEELS SHALL BE ALIGNED WITH LANE STRIPING. THIS SIGN SHALL BE LOCATED A MINIMUM END END STOP G20-2 DISTANCE OF 80 FT AND MAXIMUM OF 400 FT ROAD ROAD WORK WORK HERE ON PAST THE END OF THE DOWNSTREAM TAPER.
